findings.issue_text: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling conditional passkeys on the initial username/password login page before a user is identified and regressing passkey login
isConditionalPasskeysEnabled offers passkey authentication to preselected users without verifying they have a passwordless WebAuthn credential, exposing an unusable method during re-authentication

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled offers passkey authentication to preselected users without verifying they have a passwordless WebAuthn credential, exposing an unusable method during re-authentication

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims isConditionalPasskeysEnabled exposes an unusable method during re-authentication without verifying credentials. However, looking at the diff, the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled method in UsernamePasswordForm.java (line 160-162) checks 'webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null'. The method is used to determine whether to show passkey UI elements, not to authenticate. The tests added (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication) demonstrate that re-authentication with passkeys works correctly. The change actually enables passkey authentication during re-authentication scenarios that were previously blocked, which is the intended behavior based on the test assertions.
